overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the minutes claim was untimely and declined, posting was not required, documents need not be stored with minutes, and records-request handling falls under the Public Records Law.

allegations.summary: Minutes of four meetings allegedly failed to list the Decarbonization Roadmap among documents used at the meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Where the complaint was filed on June 22, which was more than 30 days after the Committee approved each set of minutes in open session, we find this allegation to be untimely and decline to review it.

allegations.summary: The Committee allegedly failed to post the Decarbonization Roadmap and other meeting documents to its website.
allegations.key_passage: there is no requirement in the Open Meeting Law that documents be posted to a website prior to or after a meeting.

allegations.summary: The Committee allegedly excluded the Decarbonization Roadmap and other documents from the official record of four open session meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, although documents and other exhibits, such as photographs, recordings or maps, used by the body at an open session shall, along with the minutes, be part of the official record of the session, such documents and exhibits do not need to be attached to or physically stored with the minutes.

allegations.summary: The Committee allegedly failed to provide the Roadmap in response to a public records request for meeting documents.
allegations.key_passage: Failure to timely respond to requests for documents other than minutes concerns a potential violation of the Public Records Law, rather than the Open Meeting Law.
